result.title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context
result.summary: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Generating and parsing a separate textual response for each structured question adds latency between visual evidence and usable decisions. Building on the System One paradigm, we introduce PathoJev, a pathology model that directly predicts answer probabilities for whole-slide and region-level assessment. PathoJev encodes each slide once and evaluates independent question suffixes in batches over the shared visual context. Reusing the hybrid backbone's recurrent states further limits the computation that grows with slide-context length for each additional question. Across three whole-slide benchmarks, the 9B and 27B models achieve mean accuracies of 77.2% and 78.1%, exceeding SlideChat by 5.4 and 6.3 percentage points. Both scales also maintain competitive accuracy on five ROI benchmarks. On WSI-Bench, the 9B model runs 9.1x faster than SlideChat. Shared context accelerates eight-question workloads by 6.9x and 5.9x over separate prefix encoding, rising to 11.2x and 8.9x for 64 questions. These results provide a reusable probabilistic interface for combining multiple visual judgments in whole-slide and local tissue assessment. Code: https://github.com/ChyaZhang/PathoJev.

AI.brief_summary: PathoJev 面向病理全切片与 ROI 判读，对同一视觉上下文只编码一次，批量并行评估多个问题的答案概率，并复用混合骨干的循环状态以抑制随上下文长度与问题数增长的计算量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其共享视觉上下文加批量问题后缀、复用循环状态的做法，可能为 LVR 中多查询共享视觉证据、缓存与注意力结构对 latent 相似度及推理成本的影响提供可核查线索。
